30: # OpenDub — local video dubbing MVP
31: 
32: The core product currently implements **Build Step 1: a Gradio dubbing MVP**. It accepts a video/audio file, transcribes speech, translates into one selected target language, creates speech, aligns it to the original segment slots, and exports MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT. A separate local FastAPI job API is also available as an early backend step. The stack uses free/open-source software and does not require API keys or paid APIs.
33: 
34: The full multi-user Next.js dashboard and production backend described in the original product brief are not part of this prototype. There are no user accounts, durable jobs, or daily quota enforcement. Treat the current release as a local pipeline prototype, not a hosted service.
35: 
36: ## Pipeline and limitations
37: 
38: - FFmpeg extracts audio and creates the final mux. Audio-only inputs receive a black still-video track in the MP4.
39: - faster-whisper provides speech transcription and timestamps. Whisper model weights download on first use.
40: - NLLB-200 distilled 600M translates each segment locally. Its model weights are several GB and need to download on first use; CPU translation can be slow.
41: - Microsoft Edge TTS is free to use through the `edge-tts` client, but it requires an internet connection and relies on Microsoft's service. It is not offline or guaranteed by an SLA.
42: - Demucs vocal/background separation is optional and disabled by default; enabling it downloads model weights and is slow on CPU. When enabled, the non-vocal stem is used as the music bed.
43: - There is no voice cloning in this MVP. No source-speaker diarization is performed; a target voice gender is selectable.
44: - Timing is fit to transcription slots. Very long translations are shortened and, as a last resort, trimmed to prevent overlap. Review the generated translation and subtitles before publishing.
45: - The UI limits media to 60 minutes. Model memory and runtime requirements vary significantly; on CPU, start with a short clip and Whisper `tiny` or `base`.
46: 
47: ## Local setup (recommended)
48: 
49: Requirements: 64-bit Linux/macOS, CPython 3.11, FFmpeg (including `ffprobe`), and enough disk for model downloads. GPU is optional.
50: 
51: ### 1. Install FFmpeg
52: 
53: Ubuntu/Debian:
54: 
55: ```bash
56: sudo apt-get update
57: sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg
58: ```
59: 
60: macOS with Homebrew:
61: 
62: ```bash
63: brew install ffmpeg
64: ```
65: 
66: Confirm both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are on `PATH`:
67: 
68: ```bash
69: ffmpeg -version
70: ffprobe -version
71: ```
72: 
73: ### 2. Install and start
74: 
75: ```bash
76: python3.11 -m venv .venv
77: source .venv/bin/activate
78: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
79: pip install -r requirements.txt
80: cp .env.example .env  # optional; values can also be exported in your shell
81: HOST=127.0.0.1 python app.py
82: ```
83: 
84: Open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. No `.env` file is needed for the default configuration. Binding to `127.0.0.1` keeps the Gradio app reachable only from your machine; set `HOST=0.0.0.0` only when a container or trusted network needs to reach it. On Windows, install a CPython 3.11 environment and an FFmpeg build, then activate the venv and run `$env:HOST="127.0.0.1"; python app.py` in PowerShell.
85: 
86: ### 3. Test the pipeline
87: 
88: 1. Start with a short (10–30 second) video or audio clip with clear speech.
89: 2. Upload it, leave source language on Auto-detect, choose a target, then click **Create dub**.
90: 3. Wait for the first-run Whisper and NLLB model downloads; these are cached for later runs.
91: 4. Check the MP4 and MP3, and open the SRT/VTT to verify transcript, translation, and timing.
92: 5. Enable “Preserve background music” on a second run only after Demucs has installed successfully; CPU separation can take a while.
93: 
94: Generated results are stored under `outputs/<job-id>/`. Temporary working audio is removed when a job ends. Delete `outputs/` yourself when you no longer need the results.
95: 
96: ### Useful settings
97: 
98: Copy `.env.example` to `.env` as a reference and export the values before launching (the app does not load dotenv automatically):
99: 
100: ```bash
101: export WHISPER_DEVICE=cpu
102: export WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE=int8
103: export PORT=7860
104: python app.py
105: ```
106: 
107: For CUDA, install a PyTorch build compatible with your CUDA runtime and set `WHISPER_DEVICE=cuda` and an appropriate compute type (for example `float16`). Translation uses the Transformers/PyTorch default device and can require substantial CPU/RAM. Choose `tiny` or `base` Whisper in the UI for quicker local tests.
108: 
109: ## Local FastAPI job API (prototype)
110: 
111: A separate FastAPI service wraps the same dubbing pipeline with an in-process, single-worker queue. It accepts multipart uploads up to 2 GB, returns a job ID, exposes status and stage-based progress milestones (`progress_percent` is approximate, not a measure of work within a stage), and provides MP4/MP3/SRT/VTT download routes. Jobs and queue state are held in memory and disappear when the process restarts; outputs remain under `outputs/`.
112: 
113: Start it from the activated environment after installing requirements:
114: 
115: ```bash
116: python api.py
117: ```
118: 
119: Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000/> for the connected studio UI or <http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs> for interactive API documentation. The main routes are `POST /dub`, `GET /dub/{job_id}`, and `GET /api/jobs/{job_id}/files/{kind}` where `kind` is `video`, `audio`, `srt`, or `vtt`. The older `/api/jobs` submission/status routes remain aliases. The upload form fields use the same language, voice, glossary, speed, and Whisper choices as the Gradio app.
120: 
121: This is still a local prototype, **not a secure public multi-user service**: it has no authentication, durable job store, daily quota enforcement, or cross-process worker. Keep the default localhost binding. Before exposing it publicly, add authentication, request/rate limits, durable queue/storage, and deployment-specific upload limits.
122: 
123: ## Docker
124: 
125: The image includes FFmpeg and installs the Python dependencies. Model weights are not baked into the image:
126: 
127: ```bash
128: docker build -t opendub .
129: docker run --rm -p 7860:7860 \
130:   -v "$PWD/outputs:/app/outputs" \
131:   -v "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
132:   opendub
133: ```
134: 
135: Then open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. The first run downloads models into the mounted cache. Docker builds and model downloads are large.
136: 
137: ## Google Colab (ready-to-run notebook)
138: 
139: Open [`opendub_colab.ipynb`](opendub_colab.ipynb) in Google Colab and run its cells from top to bottom. The notebook clones this repository, installs FFmpeg and Python requirements, selects CPU/GPU inference settings, and launches the Gradio app with `share=True`. Colab displays a temporary public Gradio URL after launch. Use that URL to upload a short clip and download the generated MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT files.
140: 
141: The first job downloads model weights; NLLB-200 is several GB. The notebook includes an optional model-preload cell, disabled by default. Free GPU availability, RAM, disk, and session duration are not guaranteed. Outputs and cached models in a free Colab runtime are temporary, so download results before disconnecting. A share URL is accessible to anyone who has it: do not upload private media or leave a session running unattended.
142: 
143: ## Hugging Face Spaces
144: 
145: This repository includes the Gradio Space metadata in `README.md`, the Space entry point `app.py`, Python dependencies in `requirements.txt`, and system dependencies in `packages.txt` (`ffmpeg` and `libsndfile1`). To create a Space:
146: 
147: 1. On Hugging Face, create a new Space and choose the **Gradio** SDK. A free CPU tier is sufficient to launch the UI but may not have enough memory, disk, or compute for model downloads and inference.
148: 2. Add or upload this repository's `app.py`, `requirements.txt`, `packages.txt`, and `README.md` to the Space. Keep the rest of the Python files in the same root if using the complete repository. The README front matter selects `app.py` as the entry point.
149: 3. Let the Space build. It installs `requirements.txt` and the apt packages listed in `packages.txt`; the app listens on port `7860` and binds to the Space container interface.
150: 4. Open the Space and test first with a short clip and Whisper `tiny` or `base`. Model weights download on the first job. Enable persistent storage only if you understand its cost; free Space storage and generated files may be ephemeral.
151: 
152: A public Space is a public service. This prototype does not provide accounts, authentication, durable job isolation, or quotas. Do not use it for sensitive media. The separate FastAPI service is intended for local use and should not be exposed publicly without adding appropriate access controls.
153: 
154: This project does not create or manage a hosting account. Check current provider limits and relevant hosting, model, dependency, and Edge TTS terms before deploying. Free hardware and session availability are not guaranteed.
155: 
156: ## Structure
157: 
158: ```text
159: .
160: ├── app.py              # Gradio UI and end-to-end dubbing pipeline
161: ├── api.py              # Local FastAPI job API
162: ├── requirements.txt
163: ├── Dockerfile
164: ├── .env.example
165: └── outputs/            # Created automatically; completed downloads
166: ```
167: 
168: ## License and service notes
169: 
170: This project is a prototype. Check the licenses of the chosen models, dependencies, and the Edge TTS service for your use case. Media processing is local except Edge TTS speech generation. The app does not upload media to a third-party API by itself, but text supplied to Edge TTS is sent to Microsoft's service.

"""OpenDub: Gradio inference backend for the browser-based dubbing studio.

The browser extracts a mono WAV and keeps the original media local. This backend
returns dubbed audio, translated subtitles, and text; the browser muxes MP4 locally
so the source video is never uploaded to the inference backend.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import threading
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterator

import gradio as gr

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUTPUT_DIR = Path(os.getenv("OUTPUT_DIR", ROOT / "outputs")).resolve()
OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
MAX_BYTES = 200 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_SECONDS = 10 * 60
MAX_TTS_CONCURRENCY = 8
WHISPER_MODEL = "small"
TRANSLATION_MODEL = "facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M"

LANGUAGES = {
    "Hindi": ("hin_Deva", "hi", "hi-IN-SwaraNeural", "hi-IN-MadhurNeural"),
    "Kannada": ("kan_Knda", "kn", "kn-IN-SapnaNeural", "kn-IN-GaganNeural"),
    "Tamil": ("tam_Taml", "ta", "ta-IN-PallaviNeural", "ta-IN-ValluvarNeural"),
    "Telugu": ("tel_Telu", "te", "te-IN-ShrutiNeural", "te-IN-MohanNeural"),
    "Malayalam": ("mal_Mlym", "ml", "ml-IN-SobhanaNeural", "ml-IN-MidhunNeural"),
    "Marathi": ("mar_Deva", "mr", "mr-IN-AarohiNeural", "mr-IN-ManoharNeural"),
    "Bengali": ("ben_Beng", "bn", "bn-IN-TanishaaNeural", "bn-IN-BashkarNeural"),
    "Gujarati": ("guj_Gujr", "gu", "gu-IN-DhwaniNeural", "gu-IN-NiranjanNeural"),
    "English": ("eng_Latn", "en", "en-US-AriaNeural", "en-US-GuyNeural"),
}
SOURCE_CODES = {"Auto-detect": None, **{name: data[1] for name, data in LANGUAGES.items()}}
NLLB_CODES = {data[1]: data[0] for data in LANGUAGES.values()}

_whisper_lock = threading.Lock()
_whisper_models = {}
_translator = None
_translation_lock = threading.Lock()


def _run(command: list[str], timeout: int = 900) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Required program is missing: {command[0]}. Install FFmpeg and ffprobe.") from exc
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
        raise RuntimeError("Media processing timed out. Retry with a shorter clip.") from exc
    if result.returncode:
        detail = (result.stderr or result.stdout)[-1800:]
        raise RuntimeError(f"{command[0]} failed: {detail}")
    return result


def _duration(path: Path) -> float:
    result = _run([
        "ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
        "-of", "default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1", str(path),
    ])
    try:
        duration = float(result.stdout.strip())
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError("Could not read audio duration. Make sure the WAV is valid.") from exc
    if duration <= 0 or duration > MAX_SECONDS:
        raise RuntimeError("Clips must be longer than zero and no more than 10 minutes.")
    return duration


def _cuda_available() -> bool:
    try:
        import torch
        return torch.cuda.is_available()
    except Exception:
        return False


def _transcribe(audio_path: Path, source_language: str):
    from faster_whisper import WhisperModel

    use_gpu = os.getenv("WHISPER_DEVICE", "cuda" if _cuda_available() else "cpu") == "cuda"
    compute = "float16" if use_gpu else "int8"
    cache_key = (WHISPER_MODEL, "cuda" if use_gpu else "cpu", compute)
    with _whisper_lock:
        model = _whisper_models.get(cache_key)
        if model is None:
            model = WhisperModel(WHISPER_MODEL, device=cache_key[1], compute_type=compute)
            _whisper_models[cache_key] = model
    language = SOURCE_CODES.get(source_language)
    segments, info = model.transcribe(str(audio_path), language=language, beam_size=1, vad_filter=True)
    rows = [
        (max(0.0, float(seg.start)), max(0.05, float(seg.end)), (seg.text or "").strip())
        for seg in segments if (seg.text or "").strip()
    ]
    return rows, info.language


def _get_translator():
    global _translator
    with _translation_lock:
        if _translator is None:
            import torch
            from transformers import AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM, AutoTokenizer

            model_id = os.getenv("TRANSLATION_MODEL", TRANSLATION_MODEL)
            tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
            model = AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM.from_pretrained(model_id)
            # CUDA/T4 inference uses fp16; CPU fallback stays fp32 for compatibility.
            if torch.cuda.is_available():
                model = model.to("cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
            model.eval()
            _translator = (tokenizer, model, torch)
    return _translator


def _translate_batch(texts: list[str], source_code: str, target_code: str) -> list[str]:
    tokenizer, model, torch = _get_translator()
    tokenizer.src_lang = source_code
    results = []
    for offset in range(0, len(texts), 16):
        batch = texts[offset:offset + 16]
        encoded = tokenizer(batch, return_tensors="pt", padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=512)
        device = next(model.parameters()).device
        encoded = {key: value.to(device) for key, value in encoded.items()}
        with torch.inference_mode():
            tokens = model.generate(
                **encoded,
                forced_bos_token_id=tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(target_code),
                max_new_tokens=256,
                num_beams=2,
            )
        results.extend(text.strip() for text in tokenizer.batch_decode(tokens, skip_special_tokens=True))
    return results


def _srt_time(seconds: float) -> str:
    millis = max(0, round(seconds * 1000))
    hours, millis = divmod(millis, 3_600_000)
    minutes, millis = divmod(millis, 60_000)
    whole, millis = divmod(millis, 1000)
    return f"{hours:02}:{minutes:02}:{whole:02},{millis:03}"


def _write_srt(rows, path: Path) -> None:
    entries = [
        f"{index}\n{_srt_time(start)} --> {_srt_time(end)}\n{text}"
        for index, (start, end, text) in enumerate(rows, 1)
    ]
    path.write_text("\n\n".join(entries) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


async def _synthesize(texts: list[str], voice: str, rate: int, temp_dir: Path) -> list[Path]:
    import edge_tts

    semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(MAX_TTS_CONCURRENCY)

    async def one(index: int, text: str) -> Path:
        path = temp_dir / f"voice-{index:05}.mp3"
        async with semaphore:
            await edge_tts.Communicate(text, voice, rate=f"{rate:+d}%").save(str(path))
        return path

    return await asyncio.gather(*(one(i, text) for i, text in enumerate(texts)))


def _atempo_filter(factor: float) -> str:
    return f"atempo={min(1.6, max(0.5, factor)):.5f}"


def dub_audio(audio_file, target_language: str, source_language: str,
              voice_gender: str, speech_speed: float, keep_background: bool) -> Iterator:
    """Yield stage messages followed by dubbed audio, SRT, and translated text."""
    outputs = (None, None, None)
    job_dir = None
    temp_dir = None
    try:
        if not audio_file:
            raise RuntimeError("Choose a media file and allow browser audio extraction before starting.")
        audio_path = Path(audio_file)
        if not audio_path.is_file():
            raise RuntimeError("The extracted audio expired. Re-select the media and retry.")
        if audio_path.stat().st_size > MAX_BYTES:
            raise RuntimeError("Extracted audio is over 200 MB. Choose a smaller clip.")
        if target_language not in LANGUAGES or source_language not in SOURCE_CODES:
            raise RuntimeError("Select a supported source and target language.")
        if voice_gender not in {"Female", "Male"}:
            raise RuntimeError("Select a voice gender.")
        rate = max(-20, min(20, int(speech_speed)))
        duration = _duration(audio_path)
        job_dir = OUTPUT_DIR / uuid.uuid4().hex
        job_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        temp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="opendub-"))

        yield "Transcribe: loading cached faster-whisper small model…", *outputs
        raw, detected = _transcribe(audio_path, source_language)
        rows = []
        for start, end, text in raw:
            start = min(start, duration)
            end = min(max(end, start + 0.05), duration)
            if end > start:
                rows.append((start, end, text))
        if not rows:
            raise RuntimeError("No speech was detected. Try a clearer clip with audible speech.")
        source_code = NLLB_CODES.get(detected)
        if not source_code:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Detected language '{detected}' is not supported by this translation model. "
                "Choose a source language manually and retry."
            )

        yield "Translate: NLLB-200 distilled 600M, batches of 16…", *outputs
        target_code = LANGUAGES[target_language][0]
        translated = _translate_batch([row[2] for row in rows], source_code, target_code)
        translated_rows = [
            (start, end, text or original)
            for (start, end, original), text in zip(rows, translated)
        ]
        voice = LANGUAGES[target_language][2 if voice_gender == "Female" else 3]

        yield "Voice: generating segments in parallel (maximum 8)…", *outputs
        voice_paths = asyncio.run(_synthesize([row[2] for row in translated_rows], voice, rate, temp_dir))
        from pydub import AudioSegment

        mixed = AudioSegment.silent(duration=round(duration * 1000), frame_rate=24000).set_channels(1)
        if keep_background:
            source_bed = AudioSegment.from_file(audio_path).set_frame_rate(24000).set_channels(1)
            source_bed = source_bed[:len(mixed)]
            if len(source_bed) < len(mixed):
                source_bed += AudioSegment.silent(duration=len(mixed) - len(source_bed), frame_rate=24000)
            mixed = source_bed.apply_gain(-18).overlay(mixed)

        yield "Sync: fitting each voice clip with FFmpeg atempo (maximum 1.6x)…", *outputs
        for (start, end, _), path in zip(translated_rows, voice_paths):
            slot_ms = max(80, round((end - start) * 1000))
            clip = AudioSegment.from_file(path)
            if len(clip) > slot_ms:
                factor = min(1.6, len(clip) / slot_ms)
                fitted = temp_dir / f"fit-{path.stem}.mp3"
                _run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(path), "-filter:a", _atempo_filter(factor), str(fitted)], timeout=120)
                clip = AudioSegment.from_file(fitted)
            clip = clip.set_frame_rate(24000).set_channels(1)[:slot_ms]
            mixed = mixed.overlay(clip, position=round(start * 1000))

        yield "Export: writing MP3, SRT, and translated text…", *outputs
        stem = f"dub-{target_language.lower()}"
        mp3_path = job_dir / f"{stem}.mp3"
        _run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(temp_dir / "dubbed.wav"), "-codec:a", "libmp3lame", "-q:a", "2", str(mp3_path)], timeout=300)
        srt_path = job_dir / f"{stem}.srt"
        _write_srt(translated_rows, srt_path)
        text_path = job_dir / f"{stem}.txt"
        text_path.write_text("\n\n".join(row[2] for row in translated_rows) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        mixed.export(temp_dir / "dubbed.wav", format="wav")

        yield f"Export: ready for local MP4 mux; {len(rows)} translated segments.", mp3_path, srt_path, text_path
    except Exception as exc:
        yield f"ERROR: {exc}\n\nSelect Retry to run the job again.", *outputs
    finally:
        if temp_dir:
            shutil.rmtree(temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)


def build_app():
    with gr.Blocks(title="OpenDub — Free AI Dubbing", theme=gr.themes.Soft(primary_hue="indigo")) as demo:
        gr.Markdown(
            "# 🎙️ OpenDub\nFree AI dubbing for short clips. Your browser extracts and keeps the original media local; "
            "only extracted audio is sent to this backend. The browser creates the final MP4."
        )
        audio = gr.File(label="Extracted mono WAV (max 200 MB, 10 minutes)", file_types=[".wav"], type="filepath")
        with gr.Row():
            source = gr.Dropdown(list(SOURCE_CODES), value="Auto-detect", label="Source language")
            target = gr.Dropdown(list(LANGUAGES), value="Hindi", label="Target language")
            gender = gr.Radio(["Female", "Male"], value="Female", label="Voice gender")
        with gr.Row():
            speed = gr.Slider(-20, 20, value=0, step=5, label="Voice rate (%)")
            background = gr.Checkbox(value=False, label="Keep original background audio (lowered under dub)")
        run = gr.Button("Create dub", variant="primary")
        status = gr.Markdown("Ready. Browser extraction and first-time model downloads may take a little time.")
        with gr.Row():
            audio_out = gr.File(label="Dubbed MP3")
            srt_out = gr.File(label="Subtitles (SRT)")
            text_out = gr.File(label="Translated text")
        run.click(
            dub_audio,
            [audio, target, source, gender, speed, background],
            [status, audio_out, srt_out, text_out],
            concurrency_limit=1,
            time_limit=7200,
        )
        gr.Markdown(
            "Privacy note: only extracted audio is uploaded to this backend. Edge TTS sends translated text to Microsoft's service. "
            "Temporary working files are deleted; completed output files remain in the outputs directory."
        )
    return demo


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = build_app().queue(default_concurrency_limit=1, max_size=8)
    app.launch(
        server_name=os.getenv("HOST", "0.0.0.0"),
        server_port=int(os.getenv("PORT", "7860")),
        share=os.getenv("SHARE", "false").lower() == "true",
        show_error=True,
    )

## Objective
- Replace the dubbing prototype with a free AI video-dubbing app: a Gradio backend and separate mobile-first browser frontend.
- Deliver complete code, dependencies, and a five-step setup guide; test with a 30-second clip.

## Requirements
- Gradio backend for Colab T4 or Hugging Face Spaces, launched with `share=True`; frontend saves backend URL in `localStorage`, uses `@gradio/client`, and offers **Test connection**.
- Use faster-whisper `small` with GPU float16, beam size 1, and VAD; NLLB-200 distilled 600M in fp16 with batches of 16 and 2 beams; cache models; run Edge TTS in parallel, capped at 8.
- Extract audio in-browser with ffmpeg.wasm; use FFmpeg `atempo` up to 1.6x and pydub overlays; mux MP4 while copying video without re-encoding.
- Show progress for Extract, Transcribe, Translate, Voice, Sync, and Export; handle timeouts and clear errors, provide Retry, and end progress in a terminal state.
- Warn for files over 200 MB or longer than 10 minutes.
- Support video/audio, auto or selected source language, target language, voice gender, speed, and keep-background toggle; languages: Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, English.
- Output dubbed MP4, MP3, SRT, and translated text. Use free/open-source tools, no paid APIs; delete temporary files.
- Do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Keep the original media in the browser: upload only extracted WAV to the backend, then mux the downloaded dub with the local original media in the browser. This resolves the earlier audio-only upload conflict while preserving the original video stream.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced `dist/index.html` with a responsive frontend draft for media selection, settings, backend URL storage/testing, ffmpeg.wasm extraction, progress, and downloads.
- Refactored `app.py` to an audio-only Gradio `dub_audio` pipeline returning MP3, SRT, and translated text; browser is expected to create MP4.

### Active
- Integrate frontend with the new `/dub_audio` endpoint; implement browser-side MP4 mux and output handling.
- Fix backend export ordering: `ffmpeg` reads `temp_dir/dubbed.wav` before `mixed.export(...)` currently writes it.
- Align `requirements.txt`, `opendub_colab.ipynb`, and `README.md` to the required architecture and five-step setup guide; remove stale FastAPI/Demucs documentation.
- Run static checks and test with a 30-second clip when dependencies are available.

### Blocked
- End-to-end testing is unavailable in the current environment: Python is 3.14.4, and `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` are not installed; project requirements target Python 3.11.

## Next Move
1. Fix WAV export ordering in `app.py`.
2. Update frontend to upload only extracted WAV to `/dub_audio`, consume its three file outputs, and mux MP4 locally with ffmpeg.wasm.
3. Align dependencies, notebook, and README; run static checks and test in a compatible environment with FFmpeg.

## Relevant Files
- `app.py`: New audio-only Gradio backend; currently has an export-order bug.
- `dist/index.html`: Frontend draft still targets the old `/dub_media` interface and expects backend MP4 output.
- `requirements.txt`: Still includes stale FastAPI and Demucs dependencies.
- `opendub_colab.ipynb`: Launcher and notes need alignment with the new architecture.
- `README.md`: Setup and architecture documentation remains stale.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `README.md` is modified and several project files are untracked.
- The backend and frontend have not been tested end to end.
- The backend now returns status, MP3, SRT, and TXT; it no longer accepts the original media or produces MP4.

30: # OpenDub — local video dubbing MVP
31: 
32: The core product currently implements **Build Step 1: a Gradio dubbing MVP**. It accepts a video/audio file, transcribes speech, translates into one selected target language, creates speech, aligns it to the original segment slots, and exports MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT. A separate local FastAPI job API is also available as an early backend step. The stack uses free/open-source software and does not require API keys or paid APIs.
33: 
34: The full multi-user Next.js dashboard and production backend described in the original product brief are not part of this prototype. There are no user accounts, durable jobs, or daily quota enforcement. Treat the current release as a local pipeline prototype, not a hosted service.
35: 
36: ## Pipeline and limitations
37: 
38: - FFmpeg extracts audio and creates the final mux. Audio-only inputs receive a black still-video track in the MP4.
39: - faster-whisper provides speech transcription and timestamps. Whisper model weights download on first use.
40: - NLLB-200 distilled 600M translates each segment locally. Its model weights are several GB and need to download on first use; CPU translation can be slow.
41: - Microsoft Edge TTS is free to use through the `edge-tts` client, but it requires an internet connection and relies on Microsoft's service. It is not offline or guaranteed by an SLA.
42: - Demucs vocal/background separation is optional and disabled by default; enabling it downloads model weights and is slow on CPU. When enabled, the non-vocal stem is used as the music bed.
43: - There is no voice cloning in this MVP. No source-speaker diarization is performed; a target voice gender is selectable.
44: - Timing is fit to transcription slots. Very long translations are shortened and, as a last resort, trimmed to prevent overlap. Review the generated translation and subtitles before publishing.
45: - The UI limits media to 60 minutes. Model memory and runtime requirements vary significantly; on CPU, start with a short clip and Whisper `tiny` or `base`.
46: 
47: ## Local setup (recommended)
48: 
49: Requirements: 64-bit Linux/macOS, CPython 3.11, FFmpeg (including `ffprobe`), and enough disk for model downloads. GPU is optional.
50: 
51: ### 1. Install FFmpeg
52: 
53: Ubuntu/Debian:
54: 
55: ```bash
56: sudo apt-get update
57: sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg
58: ```
59: 
60: macOS with Homebrew:
61: 
62: ```bash
63: brew install ffmpeg
64: ```
65: 
66: Confirm both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are on `PATH`:
67: 
68: ```bash
69: ffmpeg -version
70: ffprobe -version
71: ```
72: 
73: ### 2. Install and start
74: 
75: ```bash
76: python3.11 -m venv .venv
77: source .venv/bin/activate
78: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
79: pip install -r requirements.txt
80: cp .env.example .env  # optional; values can also be exported in your shell
81: HOST=127.0.0.1 python app.py
82: ```
83: 
84: Open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. No `.env` file is needed for the default configuration. Binding to `127.0.0.1` keeps the Gradio app reachable only from your machine; set `HOST=0.0.0.0` only when a container or trusted network needs to reach it. On Windows, install a CPython 3.11 environment and an FFmpeg build, then activate the venv and run `$env:HOST="127.0.0.1"; python app.py` in PowerShell.
85: 
86: ### 3. Test the pipeline
87: 
88: 1. Start with a short (10–30 second) video or audio clip with clear speech.
89: 2. Upload it, leave source language on Auto-detect, choose a target, then click **Create dub**.
90: 3. Wait for the first-run Whisper and NLLB model downloads; these are cached for later runs.
91: 4. Check the MP4 and MP3, and open the SRT/VTT to verify transcript, translation, and timing.
92: 5. Enable “Preserve background music” on a second run only after Demucs has installed successfully; CPU separation can take a while.
93: 
94: Generated results are stored under `outputs/<job-id>/`. Temporary working audio is removed when a job ends. Delete `outputs/` yourself when you no longer need the results.
95: 
96: ### Useful settings
97: 
98: Copy `.env.example` to `.env` as a reference and export the values before launching (the app does not load dotenv automatically):
99: 
100: ```bash
101: export WHISPER_DEVICE=cpu
102: export WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE=int8
103: export PORT=7860
104: python app.py
105: ```
106: 
107: For CUDA, install a PyTorch build compatible with your CUDA runtime and set `WHISPER_DEVICE=cuda` and an appropriate compute type (for example `float16`). Translation uses the Transformers/PyTorch default device and can require substantial CPU/RAM. Choose `tiny` or `base` Whisper in the UI for quicker local tests.
108: 
109: ## Local FastAPI job API (prototype)
110: 
111: A separate FastAPI service wraps the same dubbing pipeline with an in-process, single-worker queue. It accepts multipart uploads up to 2 GB, returns a job ID, exposes status and stage-based progress milestones (`progress_percent` is approximate, not a measure of work within a stage), and provides MP4/MP3/SRT/VTT download routes. Jobs and queue state are held in memory and disappear when the process restarts; outputs remain under `outputs/`.
112: 
113: Start it from the activated environment after installing requirements:
114: 
115: ```bash
116: python api.py
117: ```
118: 
119: Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000/> for the connected studio UI or <http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs> for interactive API documentation. The main routes are `POST /dub`, `GET /dub/{job_id}`, and `GET /api/jobs/{job_id}/files/{kind}` where `kind` is `video`, `audio`, `srt`, or `vtt`. The older `/api/jobs` submission/status routes remain aliases. The upload form fields use the same language, voice, glossary, speed, and Whisper choices as the Gradio app.
120: 
121: This is still a local prototype, **not a secure public multi-user service**: it has no authentication, durable job store, daily quota enforcement, or cross-process worker. Keep the default localhost binding. Before exposing it publicly, add authentication, request/rate limits, durable queue/storage, and deployment-specific upload limits.
122: 
123: ## Docker
124: 
125: The image includes FFmpeg and installs the Python dependencies. Model weights are not baked into the image:
126: 
127: ```bash
128: docker build -t opendub .
129: docker run --rm -p 7860:7860 \
130:   -v "$PWD/outputs:/app/outputs" \
131:   -v "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
132:   opendub
133: ```
134: 
135: Then open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. The first run downloads models into the mounted cache. Docker builds and model downloads are large.
136: 
137: ## Google Colab (ready-to-run notebook)
138: 
139: Open [`opendub_colab.ipynb`](opendub_colab.ipynb) in Google Colab and run its cells from top to bottom. The notebook clones this repository, installs FFmpeg and Python requirements, selects CPU/GPU inference settings, and launches the Gradio app with `share=True`. Colab displays a temporary public Gradio URL after launch. Use that URL to upload a short clip and download the generated MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT files.
140: 
141: The first job downloads model weights; NLLB-200 is several GB. The notebook includes an optional model-preload cell, disabled by default. Free GPU availability, RAM, disk, and session duration are not guaranteed. Outputs and cached models in a free Colab runtime are temporary, so download results before disconnecting. A share URL is accessible to anyone who has it: do not upload private media or leave a session running unattended.
142: 
143: ## Hugging Face Spaces
144: 
145: This repository includes the Gradio Space metadata in `README.md`, the Space entry point `app.py`, Python dependencies in `requirements.txt`, and system dependencies in `packages.txt` (`ffmpeg` and `libsndfile1`). To create a Space:
146: 
147: 1. On Hugging Face, create a new Space and choose the **Gradio** SDK. A free CPU tier is sufficient to launch the UI but may not have enough memory, disk, or compute for model downloads and inference.
148: 2. Add or upload this repository's `app.py`, `requirements.txt`, `packages.txt`, and `README.md` to the Space. Keep the rest of the Python files in the same root if using the complete repository. The README front matter selects `app.py` as the entry point.
149: 3. Let the Space build. It installs `requirements.txt` and the apt packages listed in `packages.txt`; the app listens on port `7860` and binds to the Space container interface.
150: 4. Open the Space and test first with a short clip and Whisper `tiny` or `base`. Model weights download on the first job. Enable persistent storage only if you understand its cost; free Space storage and generated files may be ephemeral.
151: 
152: A public Space is a public service. This prototype does not provide accounts, authentication, durable job isolation, or quotas. Do not use it for sensitive media. The separate FastAPI service is intended for local use and should not be exposed publicly without adding appropriate access controls.
153: 
154: This project does not create or manage a hosting account. Check current provider limits and relevant hosting, model, dependency, and Edge TTS terms before deploying. Free hardware and session availability are not guaranteed.
155:

159: .
160: ├── app.py              # Gradio UI and end-to-end dubbing pipeline
161: ├── api.py              # Local FastAPI job API
162: ├── requirements.txt

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Replace the dubbing prototype with a free AI video-dubbing app: a Gradio backend and separate mobile-first browser frontend.
- Deliver complete code, dependencies, and a five-step setup guide; test with a 30-second clip.

## Requirements
- Gradio backend for Colab T4 or Hugging Face Spaces, launched with `share=True`; frontend saves backend URL in `localStorage`, uses `@gradio/client`, and offers **Test connection**.
- Use faster-whisper `small` with GPU float16, beam size 1, and VAD; NLLB-200 distilled 600M in fp16 with batches of 16 and 2 beams; cache models; run Edge TTS in parallel, capped at 8.
- Extract audio in-browser with ffmpeg.wasm; use FFmpeg `atempo` up to 1.6x and pydub overlays; mux MP4 while copying video without re-encoding.
- Show progress for Extract, Transcribe, Translate, Voice, Sync, and Export; handle timeouts and clear errors, provide Retry, and end progress in a terminal state.
- Warn for files over 200 MB or longer than 10 minutes.
- Support video/audio, auto or selected source language, target language, voice gender, speed, and keep-background toggle; languages: Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, English.
- Output dubbed MP4, MP3, SRT, and translated text. Use free/open-source tools, no paid APIs; delete temporary files.
- Do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Keep the original media in the browser: upload only extracted WAV to the backend, then mux the downloaded dub with the local original media in the browser. This preserves the original video stream without uploading source video.

## Work State
### Completed
- Refactored `app.py` into an audio-only Gradio `dub_audio` pipeline producing MP3, SRT, and TXT; corrected WAV export ordering and ensured FFmpeg writes fitted MP3 audio.
- Updated `dist/index.html` to submit to `/dub_audio`, extract audio in-browser, locally mux MP4 with copied video, and provide progress, retry, timeout handling, backend URL storage/testing, and downloads.
- Updated the frontend privacy note to state that only extracted WAV is uploaded and MP4 muxing happens locally.

### Active
- Align `requirements.txt`, `opendub_colab.ipynb`, and `README.md` with the required architecture and five-step setup guide; remove stale FastAPI/Demucs documentation.
- Review whether to remove obsolete `api.py` so it does not reference the removed `dub_media` pipeline.
- Run static checks and test with a 30-second clip when dependencies are available.

### Blocked
- End-to-end testing is unavailable in the current environment: Python is 3.14.4, and `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` are not installed; project requirements target Python 3.11.

## Next Move
1. Align dependencies, notebook, and README with the browser-plus-Gradio architecture.
2. Remove or otherwise resolve the obsolete `api.py` and update any stale launcher references.
3. Check Python/HTML syntax and pipeline behavior; test with a 30-second clip in a compatible environment with FFmpeg.

## Relevant Files
- `app.py`: Gradio audio-only backend and dubbing pipeline.
- `dist/index.html`: Browser frontend, audio extraction, local MP4 muxing, and downloads.
- `requirements.txt`: Still includes stale FastAPI and Demucs dependencies.
- `opendub_colab.ipynb`: Launcher uses `share=True`, but notes and setup need alignment.
- `README.md`: Setup and architecture documentation remains stale.
- `api.py`: Obsolete FastAPI prototype imports removed pipeline symbols.

30: # OpenDub — local video dubbing MVP
31: 
32: The core product currently implements **Build Step 1: a Gradio dubbing MVP**. It accepts a video/audio file, transcribes speech, translates into one selected target language, creates speech, aligns it to the original segment slots, and exports MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT. A separate local FastAPI job API is also available as an early backend step. The stack uses free/open-source software and does not require API keys or paid APIs.
33: 
34: The full multi-user Next.js dashboard and production backend described in the original product brief are not part of this prototype. There are no user accounts, durable jobs, or daily quota enforcement. Treat the current release as a local pipeline prototype, not a hosted service.
35: 
36: ## Pipeline and limitations
37: 
38: - FFmpeg extracts audio and creates the final mux. Audio-only inputs receive a black still-video track in the MP4.
39: - faster-whisper provides speech transcription and timestamps. Whisper model weights download on first use.
40: - NLLB-200 distilled 600M translates each segment locally. Its model weights are several GB and need to download on first use; CPU translation can be slow.
41: - Microsoft Edge TTS is free to use through the `edge-tts` client, but it requires an internet connection and relies on Microsoft's service. It is not offline or guaranteed by an SLA.
42: - Demucs vocal/background separation is optional and disabled by default; enabling it downloads model weights and is slow on CPU. When enabled, the non-vocal stem is used as the music bed.
43: - There is no voice cloning in this MVP. No source-speaker diarization is performed; a target voice gender is selectable.
44: - Timing is fit to transcription slots. Very long translations are shortened and, as a last resort, trimmed to prevent overlap. Review the generated translation and subtitles before publishing.
45: - The UI limits media to 60 minutes. Model memory and runtime requirements vary significantly; on CPU, start with a short clip and Whisper `tiny` or `base`.
46: 
47: ## Local setup (recommended)
48: 
49: Requirements: 64-bit Linux/macOS, CPython 3.11, FFmpeg (including `ffprobe`), and enough disk for model downloads. GPU is optional.
50: 
51: ### 1. Install FFmpeg
52: 
53: Ubuntu/Debian:
54: 
55: ```bash
56: sudo apt-get update
57: sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg
58: ```
59: 
60: macOS with Homebrew:
61: 
62: ```bash
63: brew install ffmpeg
64: ```
65: 
66: Confirm both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are on `PATH`:
67: 
68: ```bash
69: ffmpeg -version
70: ffprobe -version
71: ```
72: 
73: ### 2. Install and start
74: 
75: ```bash
76: python3.11 -m venv .venv
77: source .venv/bin/activate
78: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
79: pip install -r requirements.txt
80: cp .env.example .env  # optional; values can also be exported in your shell
81: HOST=127.0.0.1 python app.py
82: ```
83: 
84: Open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. No `.env` file is needed for the default configuration. Binding to `127.0.0.1` keeps the Gradio app reachable only from your machine; set `HOST=0.0.0.0` only when a container or trusted network needs to reach it. On Windows, install a CPython 3.11 environment and an FFmpeg build, then activate the venv and run `$env:HOST="127.0.0.1"; python app.py` in PowerShell.
85: 
86: ### 3. Test the pipeline
87: 
88: 1. Start with a short (10–30 second) video or audio clip with clear speech.
89: 2. Upload it, leave source language on Auto-detect, choose a target, then click **Create dub**.
90: 3. Wait for the first-run Whisper and NLLB model downloads; these are cached for later runs.
91: 4. Check the MP4 and MP3, and open the SRT/VTT to verify transcript, translation, and timing.
92: 5. Enable “Preserve background music” on a second run only after Demucs has installed successfully; CPU separation can take a while.
93: 
94: Generated results are stored under `outputs/<job-id>/`. Temporary working audio is removed when a job ends. Delete `outputs/` yourself when you no longer need the results.
95: 
96: ### Useful settings
97: 
98: Copy `.env.example` to `.env` as a reference and export the values before launching (the app does not load dotenv automatically):
99: 
100: ```bash
101: export WHISPER_DEVICE=cpu
102: export WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE=int8
103: export PORT=7860
104: python app.py
105: ```
106: 
107: For CUDA, install a PyTorch build compatible with your CUDA runtime and set `WHISPER_DEVICE=cuda` and an appropriate compute type (for example `float16`). Translation uses the Transformers/PyTorch default device and can require substantial CPU/RAM. Choose `tiny` or `base` Whisper in the UI for quicker local tests.
108: 
109: ## Local FastAPI job API (prototype)
110: 
111: A separate FastAPI service wraps the same dubbing pipeline with an in-process, single-worker queue. It accepts multipart uploads up to 2 GB, returns a job ID, exposes status and stage-based progress milestones (`progress_percent` is approximate, not a measure of work within a stage), and provides MP4/MP3/SRT/VTT download routes. Jobs and queue state are held in memory and disappear when the process restarts; outputs remain under `outputs/`.
112: 
113: Start it from the activated environment after installing requirements:
114: 
115: ```bash
116: python api.py
117: ```
118: 
119: Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000/> for the connected studio UI or <http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs> for interactive API documentation. The main routes are `POST /dub`, `GET /dub/{job_id}`, and `GET /api/jobs/{job_id}/files/{kind}` where `kind` is `video`, `audio`, `srt`, or `vtt`. The older `/api/jobs` submission/status routes remain aliases. The upload form fields use the same language, voice, glossary, speed, and Whisper choices as the Gradio app.
120: 
121: This is still a local prototype, **not a secure public multi-user service**: it has no authentication, durable job store, daily quota enforcement, or cross-process worker. Keep the default localhost binding. Before exposing it publicly, add authentication, request/rate limits, durable queue/storage, and deployment-specific upload limits.
122: 
123: ## Docker
124: 
125: The image includes FFmpeg and installs the Python dependencies. Model weights are not baked into the image:
126: 
127: ```bash
128: docker build -t opendub .
129: docker run --rm -p 7860:7860 \
130:   -v "$PWD/outputs:/app/outputs" \
131:   -v "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
132:   opendub
133: ```
134: 
135: Then open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>. The first run downloads models into the mounted cache. Docker builds and model downloads are large.
136: 
137: ## Google Colab (ready-to-run notebook)
138: 
139: Open [`opendub_colab.ipynb`](opendub_colab.ipynb) in Google Colab and run its cells from top to bottom. The notebook clones this repository, installs FFmpeg and Python requirements, selects CPU/GPU inference settings, and launches the Gradio app with `share=True`. Colab displays a temporary public Gradio URL after launch. Use that URL to upload a short clip and download the generated MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT files.
140: 
141: The first job downloads model weights; NLLB-200 is several GB. The notebook includes an optional model-preload cell, disabled by default. Free GPU availability, RAM, disk, and session duration are not guaranteed. Outputs and cached models in a free Colab runtime are temporary, so download results before disconnecting. A share URL is accessible to anyone who has it: do not upload private media or leave a session running unattended.
142: 
143: ## Hugging Face Spaces
144: 
145: This repository includes the Gradio Space metadata in `README.md`, the Space entry point `app.py`, Python dependencies in `requirements.txt`, and system dependencies in `packages.txt` (`ffmpeg` and `libsndfile1`). To create a Space:
146: 
147: 1. On Hugging Face, create a new Space and choose the **Gradio** SDK. A free CPU tier is sufficient to launch the UI but may not have enough memory, disk, or compute for model downloads and inference.
148: 2. Add or upload this repository's `app.py`, `requirements.txt`, `packages.txt`, and `README.md` to the Space. Keep the rest of the Python files in the same root if using the complete repository. The README front matter selects `app.py` as the entry point.
149: 3. Let the Space build. It installs `requirements.txt` and the apt packages listed in `packages.txt`; the app listens on port `7860` and binds to the Space container interface.
150: 4. Open the Space and test first with a short clip and Whisper `tiny` or `base`. Model weights download on the first job. Enable persistent storage only if you understand its cost; free Space storage and generated files may be ephemeral.
151: 
152: A public Space is a public service. This prototype does not provide accounts, authentication, durable job isolation, or quotas. Do not use it for sensitive media. The separate FastAPI service is intended for local use and should not be exposed publicly without adding appropriate access controls.
153: 
154: This project does not create or manage a hosting account. Check current provider limits and relevant hosting, model, dependency, and Edge TTS terms before deploying. Free hardware and session availability are not guaranteed.
155: 
156: ## Structure
157: 
158: ```text
159: .
160: ├── app.py              # Gradio UI and end-to-end dubbing pipeline
161: ├── api.py              # Local FastAPI job API
162: ├── requirements.txt
163: ├── Dockerfile
164: ├── .env.example
165: └── outputs/            # Created automatically; completed downloads
166: ```
167: 
168: ## License and service notes
169: 
170: This project is a prototype. Check the licenses of the chosen models, dependencies, and the Edge TTS service for your use case. Media processing is local except Edge TTS speech generation. The app does not upload media to a third-party API by itself, but text supplied to Edge TTS is sent to Microsoft's service.

colorFrom: indigo

---

# OpenDub — free AI video dubbing

OpenDub is a small, free-to-run dubbing app with two separate parts:

- **Gradio backend (`app.py`)** transcribes extracted audio, translates it, creates speech, and returns MP3, SRT, and TXT files.
- **Browser studio (`dist/index.html`)** extracts audio with ffmpeg.wasm, keeps the original media on your device, then muxes the dubbed MP3 into an MP4 locally while copying the source video stream without re-encoding.

The pipeline uses faster-whisper `small`, NLLB-200 distilled 600M, and Edge TTS. No paid API keys are required. Edge TTS does require internet and sends translated text to Microsoft's service. The supported target languages are Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, and English.

## Five-step quick start (Colab backend)

1. **Open the notebook.** Open [`opendub_colab.ipynb`](https://colab.research.google.com/github/moonedition7-alt/PlayGround/blob/main/opendub_colab.ipynb) in Google Colab. In **Runtime → Change runtime type**, select a T4 GPU when one is available.
2. **Launch the backend.** Run the notebook cells from top to bottom. It installs FFmpeg and the Python dependencies, configures faster-whisper for GPU float16 (CPU int8 fallback), and launches Gradio with `share=True`. The first job downloads model weights and caches them for the session.
3. **Copy the backend URL.** Copy the public `https://....gradio.live` URL printed by the last cell. The URL is temporary and accessible to anyone who has it; do not use a shared session for private media.
4. **Open the browser studio.** Serve `dist/` locally or host it on a static web host. For local use, clone this repository on your computer and run:
   ```bash
   python3 -m http.server 3000 --directory dist
   ```
   Then open <http://localhost:3000>. The studio loads `@gradio/client` and ffmpeg.wasm from public CDNs; no frontend build step is needed.
5. **Connect and dub a test clip.** Paste the Gradio URL into **Gradio backend URL**, click **Test connection**, choose a clear 10–30 second clip, select languages and voice options, then click **Create dub**. Download the MP4, MP3, SRT, and translated TXT when complete.

The browser uploads only an extracted mono WAV to Gradio. The source video/audio stays in the browser and is used for local MP4 muxing. Files over 200 MB and clips longer than 10 minutes are rejected. The MP4 video stream is copied without re-encoding; audio-only inputs produce an MP4 container with dubbed audio but no video track.

## Local backend

Requirements: CPython 3.11, FFmpeg (including `ffprobe`), internet access for model downloads and Edge TTS, and several GB of disk/cache space. A GPU is recommended; CPU fallback is supported but can be slow.

```bash
# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg libsndfile1

python3.11 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -r requirements.txt
HOST=127.0.0.1 python app.py
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>, then use that URL as the backend URL in the studio. To make the local backend reachable from another machine, configure a trusted network or tunnel; do not expose this unauthenticated prototype publicly. To create a temporary Gradio share link, launch with `SHARE=true python app.py`.

For CUDA, install a PyTorch build compatible with your CUDA runtime. The app selects CUDA and float16 automatically when available. `WHISPER_DEVICE` and `WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE` can override the faster-whisper device and compute type. Models are cached by their respective libraries under the normal Hugging Face cache location.

## Hugging Face Spaces

This repository includes Gradio Space metadata in the README front matter, with `app.py` as the entry point. The Space installs Python dependencies from `requirements.txt` and system packages from `packages.txt` (`ffmpeg` and `libsndfile1`). A free CPU Space may not have enough memory or compute for model downloads and inference; GPU access is recommended. Once the Space is running, paste its URL into the browser studio and click **Test connection**.

The app has no user accounts, authentication, durable job isolation, or quotas. A public Space or Gradio share link can be used by anyone who can reach it. Review hosting, model, dependency, and Edge TTS terms for your use case.

## Processing details and limitations

- faster-whisper `small` uses beam size 1 and voice activity detection. Transcription and translation models are cached after loading.
- NLLB-200 distilled 600M translates in batches of 16 with two beams; GPU inference uses fp16.
- Edge TTS segment synthesis runs concurrently with a maximum of eight requests.
- FFmpeg `atempo` fits voice segments to their subtitle timing slots, capped at 1.6×; pydub places the clips and optionally overlays lowered original audio.
- The original audio option lowers and mixes the full source audio track, so original speech may remain audible. It is not source separation.
- There is no voice cloning or speaker diarization. Select a synthesized voice gender in the browser.
- Temporary work files are removed when a backend job ends. Completed MP3, SRT, and TXT files remain under `outputs/` on the backend; MP4 is assembled and downloaded by the browser.
- Browser extraction and MP4 muxing require a modern browser and network access to the ffmpeg.wasm CDN. The initial download of the FFmpeg WebAssembly core may take a little time.

## Optional Docker backend

```bash
docker build -t opendub .
docker run --rm -p 7860:7860 \
  -v "$PWD/outputs:/app/outputs" \
  -v "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
  opendub
```

The image includes FFmpeg. Models are downloaded on first use and are not baked into the image.

## Project files

```text
app.py                 Gradio audio-only inference backend
dist/index.html        Browser studio and local media processing
requirements.txt       Python backend dependencies
packages.txt           Hugging Face Spaces system dependencies
opendub_colab.ipynb    Colab launcher (Gradio share link)
Dockerfile             Optional backend container
```

This is a prototype, not a hosted commercial service. Free GPUs and session availability are not guaranteed. Check the licenses and terms of all models and services before use.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Replace the dubbing prototype with a free AI video-dubbing app: a Gradio backend and separate mobile-first browser frontend.
- Deliver complete code, dependencies, and a five-step setup guide; test with a 30-second clip.

## Requirements
- Gradio backend for Colab T4 or Hugging Face Spaces, launched with `share=True`; frontend saves backend URL in `localStorage`, uses `@gradio/client`, and offers **Test connection**.
- Use faster-whisper `small` with GPU float16, beam size 1, and VAD; NLLB-200 distilled 600M in fp16 with batches of 16 and 2 beams; cache models; run Edge TTS in parallel, capped at 8.
- Extract audio in-browser with ffmpeg.wasm; use FFmpeg `atempo` up to 1.6x and pydub overlays; mux MP4 while copying video without re-encoding.
- Show progress for Extract, Transcribe, Translate, Voice, Sync, and Export; handle timeouts and clear errors, provide Retry, and end progress in a terminal state.
- Warn for files over 200 MB or longer than 10 minutes.
- Support video/audio, auto or selected source language, target language, voice gender, speed, and keep-background toggle; languages: Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, English.
- Output dubbed MP4, MP3, SRT, and translated text. Use free/open-source tools, no paid APIs; delete temporary files.
- Do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Keep original media in the browser: upload only extracted WAV to the backend, then mux the downloaded dub with local original media in the browser.
- Remove obsolete FastAPI prototype and its dependencies; use the browser-plus-Gradio architecture.

## Work State
### Completed
- Refactored `app.py` into an audio-only Gradio `dub_audio` pipeline producing MP3, SRT, and TXT.
- Updated `dist/index.html` for WAV extraction, `/dub_audio` submission, local MP4 muxing, progress, retry, timeout handling, backend URL storage/testing, and downloads.
- Updated `requirements.txt`, `opendub_colab.ipynb`, and `README.md` for the Gradio/browser architecture and five-step setup guide.
- Deleted obsolete `api.py` and corrected the stale FastAPI reference in `start.sh`.
- Static checks passed: notebook JSON, Python syntax, JavaScript syntax, and `git diff --check`; stale FastAPI/Demucs/VTT references were not found in checked files.

### Active
- Review frontend/backend integration and run the requested 30-second end-to-end test.

### Blocked
- End-to-end test is unavailable in the current environment: Python is 3.14.4, and `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` are not installed; project requirements target Python 3.11.

## Next Move
1. Review the current frontend/backend integration and resolve any issues found.
2. Run an end-to-end test with a 30-second clip in a compatible Python 3.11 environment with FFmpeg.
3. Report test results and any remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `app.py`: Gradio audio-only backend and dubbing pipeline.
- `dist/index.html`: Browser frontend, audio extraction, local muxing, progress, and downloads.
- `requirements.txt`: Python backend dependencies.
- `opendub_colab.ipynb`: Colab launcher with `share=True`.
- `README.md`: Architecture and five-step setup instructions.
- `start.sh`: Static frontend launcher comment updated for Gradio.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; README is modified and project files including the frontend, backend, notebook, and dependencies are untracked.
- The frontend keeps the original media local; only extracted WAV is uploaded, while MP4 muxing happens in-browser.

## Objective
- Replace the dubbing prototype with a free AI video-dubbing app using a Gradio backend and a separate mobile-first browser frontend.
- Review the integration and, if possible, run a 30-second end-to-end test.

## Requirements
- Use faster-whisper `small` with GPU float16, beam size 1, and VAD; NLLB-200 distilled 600M in fp16 with batches of 16 and 2 beams; cache models; cap parallel Edge TTS at 8.
- Extract audio in-browser with ffmpeg.wasm; use FFmpeg `atempo` up to 1.6x and pydub overlays; mux MP4 locally while copying video without re-encoding.
- Show progress for Extract, Transcribe, Translate, Voice, Sync, and Export; handle timeouts and clear errors, provide Retry, and end progress in a terminal state.
- Warn about files over 200 MB or longer than 10 minutes; support audio/video, source and target languages, voice gender, speed, and keep-background toggle.
- Provide MP4, MP3, SRT, and translated text; use free/open-source tools, no paid APIs; delete temporary files.
- Gradio backend should support Colab T4 or Hugging Face Spaces, launch with `share=True`; frontend stores backend URL in `localStorage` and offers **Test connection**.
- Do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Keep original media in the browser: upload only extracted WAV; mux the downloaded dub with local original media in the browser.
- Remove the obsolete FastAPI prototype and its dependencies; use the browser-plus-Gradio architecture.

## Work State
### Completed
- Refactored `app.py` into an audio-only Gradio dubbing pipeline producing MP3, SRT, and TXT.
- Updated `dist/index.html` for WAV extraction, `/dub_audio` submission, local MP4 muxing, progress, retry, timeout handling, backend URL storage/testing, and downloads.
- Updated `requirements.txt`, `opendub_colab.ipynb`, and `README.md`; removed obsolete `api.py` and corrected the stale FastAPI reference in `start.sh`.
- Static checks passed: notebook JSON, Python syntax, JavaScript syntax, and `git diff --check`; stale FastAPI/Demucs/VTT references were not found in checked files.

### Active
- Reviewing frontend/backend integration; checked Gradio JS client documentation for `submit()` and event-stream behavior.

### Blocked
- The requested 30-second end-to-end test cannot run in the current environment: Python is 3.14.4, requirements target Python 3.11, and `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` are unavailable.

## Next Move
1. Finish reviewing integration, including how `@gradio/client` `submit()` results are consumed in `dist/index.html`.
2. Run an end-to-end test with a 30-second clip in a compatible Python 3.11 environment with FFmpeg.
3. Report test results and remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `app.py`: Gradio audio-only backend and dubbing pipeline.
- `dist/index.html`: Browser frontend, audio extraction, local muxing, progress, and downloads.
- `requirements.txt`: Python backend dependencies.
- `opendub_colab.ipynb`: Colab launcher with `share=True`.
- `README.md`: Architecture and setup instructions.
- `start.sh`: Static frontend launcher.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files include modified and untracked files.
- The frontend keeps original media local; only extracted WAV is uploaded, while MP4 muxing happens in-browser.
- Current integration uses `submission.on('data', ...)` and awaits the submission for final outputs. Gradio JS documentation presents `submit()` as an event stream; verify this consumption pattern before relying on final result handling.

11: # OpenDub — free AI video dubbing
12: 
13: OpenDub is a small, free-to-run dubbing app with two separate parts:
14: 
15: - **Gradio backend (`app.py`)** transcribes extracted audio, translates it, creates speech, and returns MP3, SRT, and TXT files.
16: - **Browser studio (`dist/index.html`)** extracts audio with ffmpeg.wasm, keeps the original media on your device, then muxes the dubbed MP3 into an MP4 locally while copying the source video stream without re-encoding.
17: 
18: The pipeline uses faster-whisper `small`, NLLB-200 distilled 600M, and Edge TTS. No paid API keys are required. Edge TTS does require internet and sends translated text to Microsoft's service. The supported target languages are Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, and English.
19: 
20: ## Five-step quick start (Colab backend)
21: 
22: 1. **Open the notebook.** Open [`opendub_colab.ipynb`](https://colab.research.google.com/github/moonedition7-alt/PlayGround/blob/main/opendub_colab.ipynb) in Google Colab. In **Runtime → Change runtime type**, select a T4 GPU when one is available.
23: 2. **Launch the backend.** Run the notebook cells from top to bottom. It installs FFmpeg and the Python dependencies, configures faster-whisper for GPU float16 (CPU int8 fallback), and launches Gradio with `share=True`. The first job downloads model weights and caches them for the session.
24: 3. **Copy the backend URL.** Copy the public `https://....gradio.live` URL printed by the last cell. The URL is temporary and accessible to anyone who has it; do not use a shared session for private media.
25: 4. **Open the browser studio.** Serve `dist/` locally or host it on a static web host. For local use, clone this repository on your computer and run:
26:    ```bash
27:    python3 -m http.server 3000 --directory dist
28:    ```
29:    Then open <http://localhost:3000>. The studio loads `@gradio/client` and ffmpeg.wasm from public CDNs; no frontend build step is needed.
30: 5. **Connect and dub a test clip.** Paste the Gradio URL into **Gradio backend URL**, click **Test connection**, choose a clear 10–30 second clip, select languages and voice options, then click **Create dub**. Download the MP4, MP3, SRT, and translated TXT when complete.
31: 
32: The browser uploads only an extracted mono WAV to Gradio. The source video/audio stays in the browser and is used for local MP4 muxing. Files over 200 MB and clips longer than 10 minutes are rejected. The MP4 video stream is copied without re-encoding; audio-only inputs produce an MP4 container with dubbed audio but no video track.
33: 
34: ## Local backend
35: 
36: Requirements: CPython 3.11, FFmpeg (including `ffprobe`), internet access for model downloads and Edge TTS, and several GB of disk/cache space. A GPU is recommended; CPU fallback is supported but can be slow.
37: 
38: ```bash
39: # Ubuntu/Debian
40: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg libsndfile1
41: 
42: python3.11 -m venv .venv
43: source .venv/bin/activate
44: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
45: pip install -r requirements.txt
46: HOST=127.0.0.1 python app.py
47: ```
48: 
49: Open <http://127.0.0.1:7860>, then use that URL as the backend URL in the studio. To make the local backend reachable from another machine, configure a trusted network or tunnel; do not expose this unauthenticated prototype publicly. To create a temporary Gradio share link, launch with `SHARE=true python app.py`.
50: 
51: For CUDA, install a PyTorch build compatible with your CUDA runtime. The app selects CUDA and float16 automatically when available. `WHISPER_DEVICE` and `WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE` can override the faster-whisper device and compute type. Models are cached by their respective libraries under the normal Hugging Face cache location.
52: 
53: ## Hugging Face Spaces
54: 
55: This repository includes Gradio Space metadata in the README front matter, with `app.py` as the entry point. The Space installs Python dependencies from `requirements.txt` and system packages from `packages.txt` (`ffmpeg` and `libsndfile1`). A free CPU Space may not have enough memory or compute for model downloads and inference; GPU access is recommended. Once the Space is running, paste its URL into the browser studio and click **Test connection**.
56: 
57: The app has no user accounts, authentication, durable job isolation, or quotas. A public Space or Gradio share link can be used by anyone who can reach it. Review hosting, model, dependency, and Edge TTS terms for your use case.
58: 
59: ## Processing details and limitations
60: 
61: - faster-whisper `small` uses beam size 1 and voice activity detection. Transcription and translation models are cached after loading.
62: - NLLB-200 distilled 600M translates in batches of 16 with two beams; GPU inference uses fp16.
63: - Edge TTS segment synthesis runs concurrently with a maximum of eight requests.
64: - FFmpeg `atempo` fits voice segments to their subtitle timing slots, capped at 1.6×; pydub places the clips and optionally overlays lowered original audio.
65: - The original audio option lowers and mixes the full source audio track, so original speech may remain audible. It is not source separation.
66: - There is no voice cloning or speaker diarization. Select a synthesized voice gender in the browser.
67: - Temporary work files are removed when a backend job ends. Completed MP3, SRT, and TXT files remain under `outputs/` on the backend; MP4 is assembled and downloaded by the browser.
68: - Browser extraction and MP4 muxing require a modern browser and network access to the ffmpeg.wasm CDN. The initial download of the FFmpeg WebAssembly core may take a little time.
